traceability.evidence:
Key implementation and test evidence for docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md:
1) Story file & dedicated tests - Story file exists: docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md - Dedicated test file for this story and its requirements: - tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts - Header explicitly links this story and requirements: - @story docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md - @req REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING - @req REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT - Jest run (npm test -- --verbose) shows the suite executed and passing: - "Auto-fix behavior (Story 008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX)" - [REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING] require-story-annotation auto-fix - valid ✓ [REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING] already annotated function is unchanged ✓ [REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING] already annotated class method is unchanged - invalid ✓ [REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING] adds @story before function declaration when missing ✓ [REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING] adds @story before function expression when missing ✓ [REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING] adds @story before class method when missing ✓ [REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING] adds @story before TS declare function when missing ✓ [REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING] adds @story before TS method signature when missing - [REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT] valid-annotation-format auto-fix - valid ✓ [REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT] already-correct story path is unchanged - invalid ✓ [REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT] adds .md extension for .story path ✓ [REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT] adds .story.md extension when missing entirely
2) REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING – auto-inserting missing @story annotations - Core rule: src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - Tagged with this story and requirement: - @story docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md - @req REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING - meta.hasSuggestions: true - meta.fixable: "code" (enables ESLint --fix) - Description explicitly mentions auto-fix: - "Require @story annotations on functions and auto-fix missing annotations where possible" - Helper implementation: src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - Defines placeholder story path and annotation template: - const STORY_PATH = "docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md"; - const ANNOTATION = `/** @story ${STORY_PATH} */`; - reportMissing(...) and reportMethod(...): - Check hasStoryAnnotation(...) first; if already annotated, do nothing (safety) - Build error with messageId: "missingStory" and data including functionName - Provide both fix and suggest entries using createAddStoryFix / createMethodFix: - fix: createAddStoryFix(resolvedTarget) - suggest: { desc: "Add JSDoc @story annotation for function '...', e.g., ${ANNOTATION}", fix: createAddStoryFix(resolvedTarget) } - Low-level fixers: src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts - createAddStoryFix(target): - Computes a safe insertion start position using target.range or its export parent.range - Returns fixer.insertTextBeforeRange([start, start], `${ANNOTATION}\n`) - Only inserts a new comment line; no runtime code is changed - createMethodFix(node): - Similar logic, inserting `${ANNOTATION}\n ` before method node - Tests in tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts validate behavior across patterns: - FunctionDeclaration: missing annotation gets a new line `/** @story ... */` inserted directly above - FunctionExpression (assigned to const): same insertion directly above - Class method: annotation inserted inside class body above method - TS declare function & TS method signature: same placeholder annotation inserted above - Valid cases confirm already-annotated functions/methods are left unchanged
3) REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT – safe @story path suffix normalization - Rule implementation: src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts - Tagged with this story and requirement: - @story docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md - @req REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT - meta.fixable: "code" with comments restricting fixes to path suffix normalization only - Key helpers: - createStoryFix(context, comment, fixed): - Uses context.getSourceCode().getText(comment) to locate "@story" - Derives just the span of the path value within the comment text - Computes fixRange based on comment.range and substring indices - Returns a factory that produces fixer.replaceTextRange(fixRange, fixed) - Returns null if it cannot safely locate the value (safety fallback) - reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix(...): - Calls createStoryFix(...) - If fixFactory is null, falls back to reportInvalidStoryFormat(...) with no fix - Otherwise reports invalidStoryFormat and attaches fix: fixFactory() - validateStoryAnnotation(...): - Normalizes and collapses the raw @story value - If the current value matches options.storyPattern, returns (no error) - If whitespace in value makes it ambiguous, reports error without fix - Calls getFixedStoryPath(collapsed) for suffix-only normalization - If getFixedStoryPath returns a new path that matches pattern, delegates to reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix (adds fix) - Otherwise reports invalid format with no fix - These functions collectively ensure: - Fixes are only applied when a simple suffix change (`.story` -> `.story.md` or no extension -> `.story.md`) is clearly safe - Only the path substring is replaced; surrounding comment text and whitespace remain unchanged (preserves formatting) - Tests in tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts confirm behavior: - Valid case: - `// @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md` remains unchanged under --fix - Invalid cases with expected output: - Input: `// @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story` Output: `// @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md` - Input: `// @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION` Output: `// @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md` - Tests assert only the suffix changes and formatting/comment structure are preserved
4) Safety, preservation, and error-handling (REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE, REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE) - For missing @story annotations (require-story-annotation): - Fixers only insert comments (ANNOTATION constant) before nodes; function bodies and signatures are untouched - reportMissing/reportMethod first call hasStoryAnnotation(...); they early-return if any @story-like text is already present, avoiding duplicate or conflicting annotations - hasStoryAnnotation(...) internally uses multiple heuristics (JSDoc, preceding comments, leadingComments, nearby text, ancestor comments) and is wrapped in try/catch to avoid throwing on malformed AST/sourceCode - For format fixes (valid-annotation-format): - createStoryFix returns null if it cannot safely parse out the path value from the comment text; in that case only an error is reported and no fix is attached - validateStoryAnnotation only attempts auto-fix when getFixedStoryPath yields a candidate that also passes pattern validation; otherwise it reports without a fix - meta.fixable is documented explicitly as limited to safe suffix normalization - Jest suite output shows multiple edge-case tests around helpers and IO edge cases passing (e.g., tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts and other helper tests), confirming the non-destructive approach and graceful handling when fixes are not possible.
5) Integration with ESLint toolchain and existing rules - require-story-annotation.ts and valid-annotation-format.ts both: - Export RuleModule objects compatible with ESLint v9 - Define meta.docs and options schemas, and set meta.fixable = "code" to opt into ESLint --fix - Use context.report with fix callbacks following standard ESLint patterns - Tests use ESLint RuleTester to validate rule behavior end-to-end: - functionRuleTester and formatRuleTester in tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts run the rules exactly as ESLint would - Tests specify expected output strings for invalid cases, so the RuleTester verifies the auto-fix integration path (not just rule logic) - Overall Jest run (npm test -- --verbose) shows all 35 suites and 264 tests passing, including this story’s auto-fix suite and numerous related rule/helper suites.
6) Documentation of auto-fix behavior (Documentation acceptance criterion) - user-docs/api-reference.md documents auto-fix capabilities for both relevant rules: - traceability/require-story-annotation section: - Explicitly states that when run with --fix, the rule "inserts a single-line placeholder JSDoc @story annotation above missing functions, methods, TypeScript declare functions, and interface method signatures using a built-in template aligned with Story 008.0. This template is currently fixed but structured for future configurability, and fixes are strictly limited to adding this placeholder annotation without altering the function body or changing any runtime behavior." - traceability/valid-annotation-format section: - Describes that when run with --fix, the rule "limits changes to safe @story path suffix normalization only—for example, adding .md when the path ends with .story, or adding .story.md when the base path has no extension—using targeted replacements implemented in the getFixedStoryPath and reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix helpers. It does not change directories, infer new story names, or modify any surrounding comment text or whitespace, in line with Story 008.0; more advanced path normalization strategies and selective toggles ... are not yet implemented." - This matches the story’s Documentation acceptance criterion and clearly communicates what --fix does and its safety constraints.
7) Requirements explicitly marked as future work - The story’s Requirements section explicitly flags the following as "Not yet implemented" and planned for future enhancement: - REQ-AUTOFIX-TEMPLATE: configurable annotation templates - REQ-AUTOFIX-SELECTIVE: selectively enabling/disabling specific fix types - Code and docs match this: there is a single built-in template (ANNOTATION constant), and there are no configuration options to toggle specific fix behaviors beyond enabling/disabling the rules themselves. - Their non-implementation is intentional and documented as out of scope for the current iteration; all currently-implemented requirements (REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING, REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT, REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE, REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE) are fully implemented and covered by tests.
traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for Story 008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX are implemented and verified: - ESLint --fix resolves common annotation violations for missing @story on functions/methods and simple @story path suffix issues via require-story-annotation and valid-annotation-format. - Auto-fixes are conservative: they only insert placeholder @story comments or adjust .story/.md suffixes inside comments, preserving runtime behavior and surrounding formatting. - Integration with ESLint is correct (meta.fixable set, standard fix callbacks); behavior is validated with ESLint RuleTester-based tests and a full Jest run, including a dedicated auto-fix suite for this story. - Error handling is robust: when a safe fix cannot be derived, the rules report detailed errors without attaching a fix. - User-facing documentation in user-docs/api-reference.md accurately describes the auto-fix behavior, scope, and safety constraints for both rules involved.
Requirements REQ-AUTOFIX-TEMPLATE and REQ-AUTOFIX-SELECTIVE are explicitly documented in the story and in the API docs as "not yet implemented" and are treated as planned future enhancements, not as part of the current acceptance scope. All currently claimed/implemented requirements for this story are satisfied with concrete code and passing tests, so this story is assessed as PASSED.
